label: first copy step (re-input of first token p/j/k/w/a), sparse content-dependent
explanation: 97% of activation mass is in the copy phase and 74% at the first copy step (recall_idx==1, prev input <DEL>, input = first original token being fed back). It is favoured when the first token is p, j, k, w or a and the token being output is c, j, t or w. It is stronger for longer sequences (L 8-9, t=8-10) and a few weak activations show up later in the copy. It essentially never fires in the original phase. But it fires on only ~0.3% of first-copy steps and ~1.4% of those with the favoured first tokens, so whether it fires depends on the sequence contents (c/j/t/g/e appearing early seemed to help) in a way no simple predicate captures. Best dev F1 ~0.15. Magnitude is highest at the first copy step for longer sequences with a p/j first token followed by c/j.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=p (+4.54), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=j (+4.54), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+4.07), in_tok=a (+3.26), in_tok=c (+2.90), prev_tok=p (+2.75). Lower it: correct=1 (-4.75), next_out=- (-2.52), orig8=- (-1.04).
